messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the RBAC rollout last night about 34 users (across two tenants) suddenly have the service-account role via SCIM. Not expected, looks like a mapping/attribute issue. :eyes:
alex: Wow. Any quick pattern? same Okta org / attribute payload?
jordy: +1, need the SCIM payload or audit lines. Could be externalId vs external_id mismatch creating a new entitlements mapping.
maria: logs attached below (redacted). Notice the SCIM PATCH where externalId flips from blank -> "svc-1234" and role map applies immediately:
```
2026-03-21T04:12:03Z scim: PATCH /Users/9876 id=9876 payload={"externalId":"svc-1234","roles":["service-account"]}
2026-03-21T04:12:03Z auth: idp_attr_map: {"idp_provider":"okta","external_id_attr":"externalId","role_map":"okta-to-redwood-v2"}
2026-03-21T04:12:03Z kms: decrypt alias/old-scim-key -> ForbiddenOperation
2026-03-21T04:12:03Z scim: retry (x3) apply-role success
```
samir: That KMS decrypt ForbiddenOperation is interesting — we rotated alias/old-scim-key last week. Are we still using the old alias in the SCIM worker env?
maria: SCIM worker config on prod shows KMS_ALIAS=alias/old-scim-key. We intended to switch to alias/redwood-scim but the helm values didn't get applied for the scim-workers group.
alex: So decrypt failed, SCIM retried, and on retry the externalId got set by a fallback path? That sounds plausible; perhaps a fallback that creates a new service account record when decrypting the previous external_id fails. Not ideal.
jordy: I dug into code: when KMS unwrap fails we call handle_missing_extid() which attempts to create a legacy extid using the idp_subject claim. If role_map evals true we end up granting service-account. That explains the spike.
maria: Confirmed. This is a logic hole introduced during the RBAC rollout to keep compatibility. We need to patch to fail hard, not fabricate extids.
samir: Immediate remediation steps I propose:
- rotate and make scim-workers use alias/redwood-scim (force deploy)
- run a targeted backfill to remove service-account role for users where extid was fabricated
- rotate any long-lived SCIM tokens created after 04:00Z
- create an audit alert for KMS decrypt failures > 5/m in 10m
alex: I can push the helm override for scim-workers now. Will push with forced rollout and verify env var.
oncall: I'm taking on the backfill script. Will run in dry-run against staging first. Command I'm planning:
```
# list users with fabricated extids
python tools/scim_find.py --since 2026-03-21T04:00:00 --filter fabricated_extid > suspects.csv
# remove service-account role where extid looks auto-generated
python tools/scim_backfill.py --file suspects.csv --action remove-role --role service-account --dry-run
```
maria: Also we need to check audit logging — some of the SCIM ops don't look like they produced an audit line in the KMS-backed audit table due to the decrypt errors. sec-bot, can you surface the audit gap?
sec-bot: Alert created: SEC-2026-031 — SCIM/KMS decrypt gap detected. Query shows ~22 operations with missing_kms_audit between 04:10Z-04:20Z. Linked to thread. :rotating_light:
jordy: For postmortem: patch handle_missing_extid() to raise and fail the SCIM op on decrypt error, add unit test, and add a migration to detect fabricated externalIds (pattern svc-\d{4} with no idp_original claim).
samir: Also we should rotate alias/old-scim-key and deprecate it to avoid accidental fallback in other services. I'll schedule KMS rotation with infra and add a playbook entry.
alex: Prod deploy done — scim-workers now point at alias/redwood-scim and restarted (pods replaced). I verified env var on 6 pods.
oncall: Dry-run backfill completed on staging; suspect list looks sane (~36 users), will run removal in 30m after final signoff.
maria: Thanks. Opening incident ticket INC-2026-045 and will start timeline. We should also communicate to affected tenants tomorrow. I'll draft the customer note.
alex: One last ask — add an alert that ties KMS ForbiddenOperation logs + sudden role grants in same minute. That would've caught this earlier.
maria: Agreed. I'll own the ticket and postmortem. Thanks folks. :thumbsup:
